text: Iftikhar Hussain Ansari (26 April 1942 – 30 September 2014), widely known as Moulvi Sahib, was a Kashmiri Shia cleric, politician, businessman, and a proponent of the Grand Ashura Procession in Kashmir. He served as a Wakil (Representative) of Ayatollah Sistani and also represented Ruhollah Khomeini. One of the leading Shia clerics in Kashmir, he maintained close relationships with scholars such as Sayyid Jawad Shahristani, Mohammad Alavi Gorgani, and Lotfollah Safi Golpaygani. He studied at Sultanul Madaris Lucknow and Hawza Najaf. He succeeded his father, Muhammad Jawad Ansari, as president of the All Jammu and Kashmir Shia Association in 1962, a position he held for life. He was a four-time Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) from the Pattan Assembly segment for the Jammu and Kashmir People's Democratic Party (PDP), and had previously been a member of the National Conference and the Indian National Congress. In 1978, he co-founded the Jammu and Kashmir People's Conference with Abdul Ghani Lone, and his son and brother are now part of the party. Ansari was also a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) for two non-consecutive terms. He gained a strong following among the Shia community due to his clerical background and served as a Minister of the State Government on multiple occasions, notably in the portfolio of Housing and Urban Development, which he revolutionized. He also focused on environmental issues and initiated a large-scale project to clean Dal Lake. His political career began in the 1960s. In 1973, he was elected as an MLC on the Indian National Congress ticket; in 1977, he switched to the Janata Party. He returned to the Indian National Congress in the 1980s and was appointed leader of the Legislature party in the Jammu and Kashmir State Assembly from 1983 to 1987. In 1996, he won the state legislative assembly elections on a Congress ticket and became a minister in the National Conference government led by Farooq Abdullah. In 2002, he joined the Jammu and Kashmir National Conference and won from Pattan; in 2006, he switched to the PDP but lost in the by-election. In 2008, he won a significant victory on a PDP ticket, reinforcing his political standing. As of 2014, he was nominated as the party's candidate for the upcoming assembly elections, reflecting his continued influence. After his death, his son, Molvi Imran Reza Ansari, who had previously been the candidate from Zadibal, was nominated for Pattan and won with a landslide victory in the 2014 J&K elections, achieving the highest margin of victory in the state's electoral history. Ansari was thrice the target of unsuccessful assassination attempts: in June 2000, he narrowly escaped a landmine explosion while addressing a religious gathering at Gund Khwaja Qasim, which killed twelve of his followers; on 1 September 2000, he was injured by an IED explosion that killed two policemen and a driver. The police suspected Hizbul Momineen, a terrorist group led by Mohammad Abbas Ansari and Ghulam Rasool Noori. Ansari died at his residence in Dar ul Jawad, Qamarwari, Srinagar, on 30 September 2014, after a prolonged battle with liver illness, having been undergoing specialized treatment in the United States. Political, religious, and social leaders expressed condolences. Hundreds of thousands of people attended his funeral, shops were closed, and all activities were suspended in Shia-dominated areas. People from all faiths and backgrounds participated in the event, and international condolences were also offered. His funeral procession was taken from his residence in Qamarwari to Imambargah Zadibal, where Namaz e Jenazah was offered. He was buried in his ancestral graveyard, Baba Mazar, Alamgari Bazar, Zadibal, Srinagar.
